analysis: All four changed files are new test files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Autopilot/: AutopilotAdoptionTests, AutopilotBusyReasonTests, AutopilotPlacementFixture and AutopilotPlacementHoldTests. No production source is changed in the supplied units, so no new runtime attack surface, key handling, attestation path or coordinator-wire behavior is introduced. The tests use inert stub engines, a scripted ProviderLoop with a nil attestation signer, a ws://127.0.0.1:0 URL, and temp directories removed in cleanup, so nothing reaches real credentials or production endpoints. They encode security-relevant expectations that the production code must satisfy: adopted inventory is withdrawn once the placement basis ends (unload, consent revoked, disabled, deselected, self-test failed, retiring, weight hash unavailable, shutdown); unadopted inventory is refused with model_not_selected when there is no lease; held slots are not evicted by slot-cap or memory pressure; holds are not recorded on builds without a verified weight hash (T-027, T-012); busy reasons are detail-gated on consent; and the snapshot omits the new capabilities and fields without consent. They also pin the wire vocabularies. Since the production implementation of autopilot adoption, holds and busy reasons is not in this batch, I could not verify that it is correct. Reviewers of the production-source units should check that the adopted-model serving gate cannot be reached without a validated placement basis, and that the hold cannot starve other tenants' loads (T-029 availability). Residual test gaps, not findings: timing-based tests (Task.sleep 20ms) could be flaky, and the native memory retained busy reason is not exercised. The patch excerpt for the hold tests was truncated, but the full text of the supplied units was reviewed.
